objectives: Describe shifting cultivation, plantation farming and livestock rearing
Name the main food and cash crops and where they grow
Describe problems of farmers and possible solutions
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify crop-zone statements (cocoa, coffee, cotton, banana, tea, rubber, oil palm) and the livestock areas, with the most recent agricultural data if the teacher adds production figures.

blocks.md: **Subsistence farming** grows food mainly for the farmer's own family, usually on small plots with simple tools such as the hoe and machete. **Commercial farming** grows crops or raises animals mainly **to sell**, often on large farms with machines, fertilisers and paid workers. In **shifting cultivation** (bush fallowing) farmers clear a plot, cultivate it for a few years, then leave it to rest and clear a new one so the soil can recover.

blocks.caption: Crops by zone
blocks.alt: Three columns listing typical crops of the south and coast, the highlands and the north.

blocks.title: Plantation farming
blocks.md: A **plantation** is a large farm growing one cash crop on a large scale, with many workers and processing on the spot. In Cameroon plantations produce **bananas**, **rubber**, **oil palm** and **tea** in the South-West, Littoral and the slopes of Mount Cameroon. Smallholders also grow **cocoa** (Centre, South, South-West), **coffee** (West and North-West highlands, and the forest zone) and **cotton** (North).

blocks.title: Food crops and livestock
blocks.md: Common food crops: **cassava, plantain, cocoyam, yams, maize, groundnuts, beans** in the south and highlands; **millet, sorghum, maize and rice** in the north. **Cattle, goats and sheep** are reared on the grasslands of the Adamawa, the North-West and the north; poultry and pigs are kept in many areas.

**Problems of farmers:** poor roads that make transport difficult and expensive, pests and diseases, falling prices of cash crops, lack of money and fertilisers, **bush fires**, soil exhaustion and climate change (late or irregular rain), and difficulty in storing and selling produce. **Solutions:** better rural roads, advice and training, **cooperatives** to sell together, improved seeds, fertiliser and irrigation, storage and processing, and fair prices.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- A cash crop is grown mainly for sale; a food crop is mainly for eating. A crop can be both (maize).
- Shifting cultivation is not the same as a nomad's life: farmers stay in the village and rotate plots.
- Do not place all crops everywhere: climate and soil decide where each grows well.

blocks.title: Example 1: type of farming
blocks.statement: A family clears a plot in the forest, grows cassava and plantain for six years and then moves to a new plot. What is this system?
steps: The family grows food for itself.
It leaves the old plot to rest.
This is shifting cultivation, a subsistence system.

blocks.title: Example 2: crop and region
blocks.statement: Which crop would you expect to see in large plantations on the slopes of Mount Cameroon, and why?
steps: The volcanic soil is fertile and rainfall is high.
Warm, wet conditions suit bananas, oil palm, rubber and tea.
blocks.answer: Bananas (or rubber, oil palm, tea), because the volcanic soil and wet climate suit them.
